title: Attention-generated dynamic local-rule Views
hypothesis: An attention-derived code that interpolates local update kernels inside the nonlinear rule preserves heldout-context rollouts with lower complete bytes than independent context rules and a better quality/compute tradeoff than attention over nonlinear branch features.
physical_object: two shared local 3x3 recurrent rule kernels
mirror_coordinate: attention score from context selects a per-context rule interpolation coordinate
controls: attention mixture over nonlinear rule features

development.selection_metric: heldout one-step and 10-step rollout nRMSE, state norm ratio, actual bytes and MACs

fresh.reason: single synthetic mechanism screen; no audit opened after native kernel interpolation comparison

success_gate: Heldout update and rollout nRMSE <=0.02; max state norm ratio <=1.1; >=25% complete byte savings vs independent; strict frontier improvement over native hypernetwork and feature-attention controls.
failure_gate: Any quality/storage/compute gate miss or exact native kernel-hypernetwork function/payload alias is FAIL for Mirror-specific value.
amendments: A01 before final scoring: corrected one-step evaluation to compare candidates against teacher outputs on the same heldout input maps. The initial mismatched-input metrics are preserved in RESULTS_INITIAL_INPUT_MISMATCH.csv and excluded; seed and gates unchanged.
boundaries: Synthetic scalar-field recurrent rules only; context and kernels are designed analytically.
No trained attention-NCA, emergent morphology, biological task or accelerator performance claim.
The dynamic basis convolution applies both basis rules each step; precomposed kernels have different compute accounting.
